validity.recommendation: Existence, gas classification, and non-duplicate status are solid -- Talen Energy Corporation's own June 2016 SEC 8-K (board-approved feasibility project) and the Pipeline News Oct-2018 trade-press directory both independently describe the same physical object: a 15-mile natural-gas lateral built to supply the Montour coal-to-gas conversion in Montour County, PA. No action needed on existence/classification/duplicate; the real findings on this row are the status and ownership concerns filed separately below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via two independent origins that both predate and postdate GEM's own citation pool. (1) Talen Energy Corporation's own 8-K exhibit (SEC EDGAR, filed 2016-06-09, dated June 7, 2016): 'the company is currently in the process of selecting a qualified third party to construct, own and operate a 15 mile lateral pipeline to bring natural gas to the 1,500 megawatt Montour plant.' (2) Pipeline News' Oct-2018 'Planned Pipelines' directory (trade-press compilation, entry revision 10/17) lists 'TALEN ENERGY CORP.' / 'Project: Montour Lateral' / 'Type: pipeline lateral' / 'Length: 15 miles' / 'Diameter: 30 inches' / 'Location: Montour County, PA' / 'Comments: Project will supply natural gas to the Montour Plant' -- an independent trade-press description of the identical project, agreeing on length, location, and purpose. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission lateral (industrial/power-plant supply line), not a gathering or distribution line -- both sources describe a dedicated point-to-point lateral to one power plant. DUPLICATE: checked the 45-row deep-sweep roster and the wider GGIT gas tab for any other PID tied to Talen Energy / Montour / Riverstone Holdings -- none found; not a duplicate. A separate SEC full-text search surfaced two 2019 UGI Corp 8-K exhibits mentioning 'Montour' -- read in full and confirmed these describe UGI's unrelated Sunbury Pipeline (a 35-mile FERC-regulated line to Hummel Station in Snyder County that merely transits Montour County geographically); correctly excluded as irrelevant, not a duplicate or cross-row lead.

validity.researcher_notes: This is the single most consequential finding on this row: a project GEM records as 'cancelled' (ShelvedYear=2018, CancelledYear=2020, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred -- i.e. nobody found a dated source for the cancellation, it was inferred from dormancy) was in fact completed, not cancelled. Timeline reconstructed from Talen's own SEC filings plus five independent, dated Marcellus Drilling News (MDN) trade-press articles: (1) June 7, 2016 -- Talen's board approves the coal-to-gas conversion project and a competitive RFP process to select a third party to build the 15-mile lateral (SEC 8-K; MDN 2016/06 article same week). (2) December 2016 -- MDN reports Talen has put the conversion 'on hold' (MDN 2016/12 article) -- this is almost certainly the event GEM's dormancy heuristic misread as a cancellation, two years before the ShelvedYear=2018 it actually recorded. (3) November 2020 -- MDN reports Talen, under Sierra Club litigation pressure, signs a pledge to convert its coal-fired plants including Montour to gas (MDN 2020/11 article) -- the project is revived, not dead. (4) February 2022 -- MDN reports Talen actively working on the Montour coal-to-gas conversion (MDN 2022/02 article). (5) August 2023 -- MDN reports the Montour PA coal-to-gas conversion is 'nearly done' (MDN 2023/08 article, title itself is the dated claim). (6) September 5, 2024 -- Talen's own SEC-filed Investor Day presentation (8-K EX-99.2) lists 'Montour PA' with Plant Type 'Natural Gas Peaker,' Dual-Unit, 1,508 MW, no longer describing it as coal -- and separately states Talen's gas fleet sits 'in the heart of the Marcellus shale near Leidy Hub.' (7) Talen's FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-26) states in its own words: 'We have already completed the conversion of our Brunner Island, Montour, and H.A. Wagner plants to lower-carbon fuels' and separately describes Montour as 'A Talen-owned and operated generation facility in Washingtonville, Pennsylvania.' Three of these seven sources are Talen's own primary-source SEC disclosures (2016, 2024, 2026) and the other four are independent trade-press reporting spanning 2016-2023 -- they agree on every turning point. I could not pin an exact in-service month/day for the lateral itself (only the plant-level conversion timeline), and I could not identify the specific third-party company the 2016 8-K says would 'construct, own and operate' the pipeline, nor confirm whether that original third-party-build plan is what was actually executed or whether Talen ended up building/operating it directly -- flagging this gap honestly rather than guessing (see the Operator fill). Per this batch's explicit guidance, a 'cancelled' project found to have actually been built is a status change to operating -- exactly this case.

validity.researcher_notes: Two independent problems with the recorded Owner1='Riverstone Holdings' 100%, neither of which I can resolve to a confident replacement. (1) The pipeline itself was never described as owned by Talen or by Talen's then-parent Riverstone: Talen's own June 2016 8-K states a yet-to-be-selected third party would 'construct, own and operate' the 15-mile lateral -- i.e. by design, someone other than Talen/Riverstone. I could not identify that third party in any source available this session. (2) Independent of the pipeline-specific question, Riverstone's ownership of Talen's corporate parent (Talen Energy Corporation, later Talen Energy Corp again post-emergence) is itself stale: Talen's own FY2025 Form 10-K states TEC's ~71 subsidiaries filed for Chapter 11 in 2022 (TEC itself joined in December 2022), the Plan of Reorganization was confirmed and 'substantially consummated on May 17, 2023,' and describes Riverstone Holdings, LLC as the entity 'which then held all of the equity in TEC' (past tense) before the restructuring -- with Riverstone receiving only a small residual stake and warrants under the plan, and 'In the third quarter 2023, Riverstone surrendered the warrants and waived its contingent right to additional TEC equity or cash' for a cash payment. So even setting aside whether Riverstone/Talen ever owned the pipeline itself, 'Riverstone Holdings 100%' is definitely not Talen's current ownership structure post-2023. I'm not proposing a replacement Owner1 because I don't have a source naming either the pipeline's actual owner or Talen's post-emergence public shareholder structure with the needed precision -- clearing the stale value is the honest outcome, not inventing a new one.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: GEM's recorded disposition (Status=cancelled, ShelvedYear=2018, CancelledYear=2020, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred -- i.e., no dated source was ever found for the cancellation, it was inferred purely from dormancy) is contradicted by a fully-reconstructed, continuously-documented timeline: proposed and board-approved June 2016 -> informally paused December 2016 (two years before the recorded ShelvedYear) -> revived November 2020 under Sierra Club settlement pressure -> actively under construction/conversion February 2022 -> 'nearly done' August 2023 -> confirmed complete in Talen's own September 2024 investor deck and February 2026 Form 10-K. This is not a dormancy-timeout judgment call (the batch's 2y-shelved/4y-cancelled rules apply to proposed/shelved rows, not to adjudicating whether an already-'cancelled' row's cancellation itself is correct) -- it is a direct factual correction: the project was completed, not cancelled. Per this batch's explicit guidance, 'a cancelled project that was actually BUILT is a status change to operating -- the most valuable finding this half of the batch can make'; P0317 is a strong, independently-sourced instance of exactly that pattern. Two honest gaps remain and are flagged rather than papered over: (1) no source pins an exact in-service month/day for the lateral itself, only the plant-level conversion's completion window (~2023), so StartYear1=2023 is a well-corroborated estimate, not a certified date; (2) the 2016 8-K's plan to have an unnamed third party 'construct, own and operate' the lateral was never confirmed as the actual execution path (vs. Talen building/operating it directly once the project resumed post-2020) -- Operator and Owner are left UNRESOLVED in fills[]/validity[] for this reason, not carried forward as Talen/Riverstone by default.

summary: Existence/classification/non-duplicate confirmed via Talen's own 2016 SEC 8-K and the Pipeline News trade-press directory. Filed a high-tier status_reviews change (cancelled -> operating, StartYear1~2023): seven convergent sources (Talen's 2016 8-K, five dated 2016-2023 Marcellus Drilling News articles, Talen's 2024 investor deck, and Talen's FY2025 10-K) show the project was paused in Dec-2016 -- not cancelled -- then revived in 2020 and completed by 2023, exactly the 'cancelled project that was actually built' pattern this batch flags as the most valuable finding available. Also filed an attribution concern: Owner1='Riverstone Holdings' 100% is unsourced for the pipeline (a 2016-8-K-named but never-identified third party was to own it) and is separately stale post-2023 Chapter 11 (Talen's own 10-K: Riverstone 'then held' the equity, surrendered its residual stake in Q3 2023). UNRESOLVED: Construction, Capacity, Pressure, FuelSource, Operator (the 2016 third-party builder was never named or confirmed as the actual executor), Owner (no current owner sourced), and Shelved/Cancelled years (no genuine shelving/cancellation milestone survives the status finding -- recommend clearing both).
